issues.description: In the solution repository the Bitmap24::resize_buffer declaration in the header does not match its definition and uses in the code. Bitmap24.hpp declares resize_buffer with three parameters (int i_width, int i_height, int stride) while the corresponding Bitmap24.cpp defines resize_buffer with two parameters (int i_width, int i_height). The example main() calls bitmap.resize_buffer(width, height) with two arguments. This mismatch (header vs. implementation vs. call sites) will cause compilation/linker errors and confuses students about the intended API.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the header, implementation and usages consistent. Preferred minimal fix: change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to match the implementation and calls (remove the extra 'int stride' parameter) so it reads: void resize_buffer(int i_width, int i_height); Alternatively, if a stride parameter is intended, update the implementation and all call sites (e.g. main.cpp and template code) to accept/pass the stride, or provide a default value in the header (int stride = 0) and implement the parameter in the .cpp accordingly. Ensure header and .cpp signatures exactly match.

issues.description: API/signature mismatch for the Bitmap24::resize_buffer routine across template and solution: the template and the implementation define/expect resize_buffer(int i_width, int i_height) (calls in main use two arguments), but the solution's header (Bitmap24.hpp) declares resize_buffer(int i_width, int i_height, int stride). This inconsistent declaration vs. definition/usage will confuse students (which signature is correct) and likely break compilation when using the solution header, creating an unnecessary mapping burden between the API and its implementation/usage.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the API consistent: update the solution header to match the implementation and usage (remove the extra 'int stride' parameter) or update the implementation and all call sites to accept/use the third parameter. Preferred minimal fix: change solution/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to declare void resize_buffer(int i_width, int i_height); so declaration, definition and calls all match and students have a consistent target.
